title: Preserve source scope across every learning-loop sink
summary: A conservative destination tier does not authorize disclosing owner-scoped source content. Review every queue, registry, artifact, receipt, audit, UI and notification sink under the original source identity.
reusable_steps: A conservative destination tier does not authorize disclosing owner-scoped source content
Review every queue, registry, artifact, receipt, audit, UI and notification sink under the original source identity
expected_outcome: Apply when a learning loop introduces scoped persistence or changes its consumers. Keep source scope separate from destination sensitivity. Resolve exact server-authorized scope before lookup; never invent a tenant, scan owner stores globally, or fall back to shared records. Reject owner, tier and physical-partition migrations before any write. Preserve personal receipts in owner storage and omit private artifact paths from shared audit metadata while retaining event correlation. If a publisher or notification consumer cannot represent source restrictions, fail closed rather than flattening them. Test actual creation and persistence, wrong-owner and wrong-scope invisibility, forged IDs, scope erasure, symlinks and absence of transient artifacts. Run final affected tests on a frozen snapshot with no concurrent gate or build writers; preserve each run report before another run overwrites it. Separate environmental failures and inconclusive attribution from genuine product regressions. An owner-store retention catalog entry marked review_required is descriptive only and does not authorize automatic deletion.
